basis: Clonal immunoglobulin deposition disorder; renal deposits cause proteinuria or impaired kidney function in nearly all patients. Other organ dysfunction is less common.

decisions.renal: involved: damaging renal deposition occurs in nearly all patients; it is an organ manifestation of the underlying monoclonal immunoglobulin disorder.

basis: Defining absence of enteric ganglion cells causes permanent loss of intestinal innervation and colonic obstruction; enterocolitis and sepsis are minority complications.

decisions.neurologic: primary: congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells is the defining lesion of peripheral autonomic nervous tissue; generalized neurologic disease is unnecessary.

basis: HHV8-associated vascular malignancy predominantly affecting skin; gastrointestinal involvement is annotated 30-79%. Retinal and CNS findings do not establish direct tumor injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the defining endothelial vascular neoplasm, supported by its angiosarcoma ancestry, establishes vascular origin in addition to its usual cutaneous location.

basis: Renal bicarbonate wasting defines the acid-base disorder; cataract, glaucoma and band keratopathy each occur in 3/3, and intellectual disability in 3/3.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataract, glaucoma and band keratopathy each occur in 3/3; these are characteristic extrarenal injuries accompanying the defining renal acid-base disorder.

basis: Vertebral/rib defects define disease; CNS malformations, restrictive dysfunction and anal stenosis each occur in 1/1 assessed. Neurogenic bladder omitted by cap; tiny samples.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder occurs in 1/1 assessed but is omitted at the four-axis cap, retaining direct anorectal defects, severe CNS malformations and restrictive respiratory dysfunction.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal stenosis and ectopic anus each occur in 1/1 assessed; fixed anorectal malformations directly affect the gastrointestinal tract, although estimates are very imprecise.

basis: Intestinal defects and immunodeficiency define syndrome; supplied HPO reports developmental impairment in 6/6 and reduced visual acuity in 2/6 (~33%); small samples.

decisions.ocular: involved: reduced visual acuity documents functional visual loss in 2/6 (~33%), meeting the threshold; nystagmus alone would not establish ocular damage.

basis: Malignant sex cord-stromal tumor with Sertoli-Leydig differentiation arises from the gonadal endocrine compartment; hormone excess is not required to establish endocrine tumor origin.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: Sertoli-Leydig differentiation establishes gonadal endocrine tissue origin; absence of documented hormone excess does not make an endocrine-origin tumor purely reproductive.

basis: Intellectual disability and eczema define syndrome; thumb hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%, palatal cleft in 30-79%. Eyelid narrowing lacks established dysfunction; otitis is separately coded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: submucous cleft hard palate occurs in 30-79% and represents a direct structural oral defect.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is reported in 20/20, but the supplied evidence establishes eyelid dysmorphism without visual loss or impaired eyelid function.

basis: Localized myofibroblastic tumor usually arises in skin or subcutis; muscular and osseous sites do not establish common locomotor involvement across this concept.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: myofibroblastic differentiation does not establish locomotor tissue origin; muscle and bone are variable sites without evidence of involvement in at least 30%.

basis: Profound neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; cataracts occur in 5/5 and hearing impairment in 2/5 (40%). Precocious puberty in 1/5 is below threshold.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts in 5/5 establish common direct ocular damage; their frequency alone does not establish the eye as a primary organ of the neurodevelopmental syndrome.
